transit.name: Carbondale Circulator (RFTA)
transit.detail: Free bus between the Carbondale Park & Ride and in-town stops, every 15 minutes

transit.name: Carbondale Downtowner
transit.detail: Free on-demand rides within town limits, Mon–Fri 7 am–10 pm and Sat–Sun 9 am–10 pm

transit.name: Roaring Fork Transportation Authority (RFTA)
transit.detail: Bus service from Aspen to Glenwood Springs through the Roaring Fork Valley

founded.text: Formed in 1888 between Glenwood Springs and Aspen after the Denver & Rio Grande Railroad built its line between the two cities.

timeline.text: Land in and around Carbondale is opened to homesteaders.
Myron Thompson builds the house that is now the Thompson House Museum for his daughter Hattie and her husband Oscar Holland.
Carbondale is incorporated on April 26. William H. Dean is elected the first mayor.
The Mt. Sopris Historical Society, now the Carbondale Historical Society, is chartered.

sites.name: Thompson House Museum
sites.hours: Open by appointment for guided tours

makers.name: Carbondale Clay Center
makers.what: Ceramics, with classes and a gallery; founded in 1997

trails.name: Rio Grande Trail through Carbondale
trails.length: 3.9 miles through Carbondale; mostly asphalt, 8 to 10 feet wide
trails.trailhead: The RFTA Carbondale Park & Ride beside Highway 133, where trail parking is available; the Carbondale trailhead is by the 6th Street and Colorado Avenue bus stop
trails.season: Plowed in winter between Glenwood Springs and Carbondale after more than 3 inches of snow. Upvalley, Rock Bottom Ranch to Catherine Bridge closes from 5 pm November 30 to 5 pm April 30.
trails.dogs: On a leash at all times, and never on the wildlife section between Rock Bottom Ranch and Catherine Bridge.

trails.name: Riverfront and Stairway parks, on the Crystal River
trails.manager: Town of Carbondale Parks and Recreation
trails.size: Riverfront Park, 4.44 acres, with soft-surfaced trails; Stairway Park, 3.93 acres, with a trail, picnic table and fire pits
trails.address: Stairway Park is on Oak Run Road between Crystal Road and Greystone Drive; Riverfront Park adjoins the river south of it
trails.dogs: Not allowed: Town parks ban dogs except at Glassier Park, Hendrick Dog Park and Delaney Nature Park.
trails.fee: Organized groups, classes and teams need a Town permit.

trails.name: Triangle Park
trails.manager: Town of Carbondale Parks and Recreation
trails.size: 7.4 acres: playground, ball fields, tennis and pickleball courts, a picnic shelter, grills, restrooms and a drinking fountain
trails.address: The corner of Village Road and 8th Street
trails.dogs: Not allowed: Town parks ban dogs except at Glassier Park, Hendrick Dog Park and Delaney Nature Park.
trails.fee: Organized groups, classes and teams need a Town permit.

trails.name: Sopris Park
trails.manager: Town of Carbondale Parks and Recreation
trails.size: 3.90 acres: a bandstand, large picnic shelter, playground, sand volleyball court and restrooms
trails.address: Snowmass Drive at Second Street; the John M. Fleet pool inside it is at 685 Main Street
trails.dogs: Not allowed: Town parks ban dogs except at Glassier Park, Hendrick Dog Park and Delaney Nature Park.
trails.fee: Organized groups, classes and teams need a Town permit.
